claims.text: Adapter pattern: a class between your code and a library whose interface does not match; it implements the interface your code wants (the target interface) and translates each call into the library's calls.
claims.source_hint: glossary adapter-pattern; GoF book, Adapter pattern

claims.text: At stage-2 IEmailSender (DonHang.Domain) has one method, Task SendAsync(string toAddress, string subject, string body, CancellationToken cancellationToken); no mail library type appears in it. A CancellationToken lets the caller cancel the work, e.g. on app shutdown.
NotificationSender.SendOneAsync takes IEmailSender email and calls email.SendAsync(customer.Email, ...); NotificationSender.cs has no using for MailKit or MimeKit and names none of their types.

ServiceCollectionExtensions registers AddSingleton<IEmailSender>(new MailKitEmailSender(smtp)); SmtpSettings holds Host and Port; in Docker Compose they point at Mailpit, a fake mail server accepting email over SMTP (Smtp__Host mailpit).

MailKitEmailSender.SendAsync builds a MimeMessage (From Đơn Hàng <orders@donhang.local>, To = MailboxAddress.Parse(toAddress), Subject = subject, Body = TextPart("plain") with body), then ConnectAsync, SendAsync(message), DisconnectAsync on an SmtpClient.

MailKit's SmtpClient sends a MimeMessage over SMTP: connect (ConnectAsync), send (SendAsync(MimeMessage, CancellationToken)), disconnect (DisconnectAsync). MimeMessage is a MimeKit type; MailKit is built on MimeKit.
claims.source_hint: MailKit docs: SmtpClient.ConnectAsync / SendAsync / DisconnectAsync; README sending example

claims.text: NotificationSender, not the adapter, decides which emails go out and when to retry: it claims due rows, calls SendAsync, and on failure RecordFailure applies backoff up to MaxAttempts.
MailKitEmailSender declares no base class and implements only IEmailSender, so it cannot be passed where an SmtpClient is expected; ProductCache and the object it wraps are both IProductRepository.
claims.source_hint: C# reference: classes, inheritance and implicit reference conversions; MailKitEmailSender.cs:18; ProductCache.cs:13-14

claims.text: In DonHang.Tests, ApiFactory's ConfigureTestServices removes IEmailSender and registers FakeEmailSender, which only records (toAddress, subject) in a queue, so NotificationSender runs in tests without Mailpit.

At stage-2, `git grep -n -e "using MailKit" -e "using MimeKit" -- "*.cs"` prints MailKitEmailSender.cs lines 2-4 only; `git grep -n ": IEmailSender" -- "*.cs"` prints MailKitEmailSender.cs:18 and FakeEmailSender.cs:10.
claims.source_hint: run in examples/don-hang at stage-2 (verified locally with git grep on the tag); git-grep docs, -e and pathspec

claims.text: A decorator keeps the interface of the object it wraps and adds work; an adapter offers a different interface from the one it wraps and adds no business rule of its own.
Moving to another mail library means writing another IEmailSender implementation and registering it instead; NotificationSender, with its retry and backoff, stays unchanged.
Wrapping a library in your own interface pays off even when no switch is planned, when tests need to replace it (FakeEmailSender) and callers should read in the domain's words.
